sections.label: Police aim rehabilitating young offenders
sections.summary: Police aim mainly to rehabilitate young persons who commit offences so they can lead crime-free lives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: When Police deal with young persons who have committed offences, their main aim is to rehabilitate them, so that they can go on to lead a crime-free life.

sections.label: Police report of molestation
sections.summary: On 25 January 2016 a Police report was made by an 11-year-old girl who said she had been molested.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: On 25 January 2016, a Police report was made.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: An 11-year-old girl said that she had been molested.

sections.label: Benjamin admits touching girl
sections.summary: Benjamin admitted to Police that he intentionally touched a part of the girl's body.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Benjamin admitted to the Police that he touched a part of the girl's body and that he did so intentionally.

sections.label: Police visit school next day
sections.summary: On 26 January, the next day, Police went down to the school.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: On the next day, 26 January, Police went down to the school.

sections.label: Officer tells mother about statement
sections.summary: After conversing with his mother, the Police officer told her Benjamin would be brought to Ang Mo Kio Police Division to give a statement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: When he finished conversing with his mother, the Police officer spoke with the mother.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: He told her that Benjamin will be brought back to Ang Mo Kio Police Division to give a statement.

sections.label: Benjamin found dead; young persons figures
sections.summary: Benjamin was found dead at the foot of his block, and from 2011 to 2015, 7,196 young persons assisted Police, 70% warned, in Guidance Programme, or no further action.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: At about 4.20 pm, Benjamin was found dead at the foot of his block.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Over the last five years, from 2011 to 2015, a total of 7,196 young persons have assisted Police in investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Of these, 70%, that is, seven out of 10 were either warned or placed in a Guidance Programme or had no further action taken against them.

sections.label: Second chance for young people
sections.summary: The passage states it is better to give young people a second chance and help their rehabilitation, and that Benjamin likely would have received no more than a warning.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is better to give young people a second chance and help in their rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is likely that on the evidence available to us, Benjamin would have received no more than a warning.

sections.label: Benjamin released to his mother
sections.summary: The passage states Benjamin was released to his mother within four hours of being brought to the station.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In this case, Benjamin was released to his mother within four hours of being brought to the station.

sections.label: Review of interview Protocol
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Protocol for interviewing young persons needs amending and states the Ministry has been asked to review it.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Do we need to amend the Protocol for interviewing young persons?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I have asked my Ministry to review the Protocol.

sections.label: Facts on Benjamin's case
sections.summary: The passage states the known facts are believed accurate, nothing suggests Benjamin was mistreated by Police, and the interview cannot be said to be the specific reason for the suicide.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I have set out the facts that we know, facts which we believe are accurate.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: There is nothing so far on the evidence to suggest that Benjamin was mistreated by the Police.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: At this stage, we cannot say that the interview was the specific reason for the suicide.

sections.label: Young persons picked up yearly
sections.summary: The passage states that every year more than 1,300 young persons, students and others, are picked up.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Every year, we pick up more than 1,300 young persons – students and also others.

sections.label: ISD interviews and radicalised boy
sections.summary: The passage states the Internal Security Department has interviewed some in that age group and that two weeks ago a 15-year-old radicalised boy from Indonesia was stopped.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Internal Security Department (ISD) has interviewed some in that age group.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And to prove the point, two weeks ago, we stopped a 15-year-old radicalised boy from Indonesia.

sections.label: Officers carried out duties faithfully
sections.summary: The speaker believes the officers carried out their duties faithfully and properly according to the rules and Protocols.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In this case, on the facts that have been given to me, I believe that they have carried out their duties faithfully and properly in accordance with the rules and the Protocols.

sections.label: Inaccurate statements about Police
sections.summary: The passage lists inaccurate statements, including that Police were not in plain clothes, intimidated Benjamin, coerced an admission, or that the girl made a false report.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Some of the inaccurate statements are as follows: (a) that the Police were not in plain clothes when they went to the school to identify Benjamin, effectively alleging that the Police were lying to Singaporeans when they put out their statement of 1 February; (b) allegations that Benjamin was interviewed and intimidated by five Police officers; (c) that he must have been coerced to make an admission to an offence that he did not commit; and (d) some have even suggested that the girl might not have been molested and might have made a false Police report.

sections.label: TOC articles false narrative
sections.summary: The passage states TOC articles conveyed a false narrative that Police lied, intimidated the boy, and pressured him to confess.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The overall narrative and impression conveyed by the various TOC articles are: (a) Police were lying; (b) Police intimidated the boy; and (c) Police put pressure on him to confess to a crime that he did not commit, allegations, implications which are false, practically leading people to conclude that Benjamin committed suicide as a result.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I have prepared a table, listing some of the articles and the falsehoods, unfounded implications which they convey.

sections.label: Ministry delayed commenting reasons
sections.summary: The Ministry did not comment substantially until now out of respect for the family and because there will be a Coroner's Inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That brings me to my fourth major point: why has my Ministry not commented substantially, particularly to correct these inaccuracies, until now?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I decided that for two reasons: (a) out respect for the family, to give them some space and time to grieve; and (b) there will be a Coroner's Inquiry (CI).

sections.label: CCTV footage withheld respect
sections.summary: The passage states matters can be dealt with at the Coroner's Inquiry and CCTV footage of the lift will not be released out of respect.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: These matters can be dealt with at the Coroner's Inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And even at this stage, I have decided that we should not release the CCTV footages of what happened in the lift, out of respect for Benjamin's memory and to help the young girl as well.

sections.label: Family requested private inquiry
sections.summary: The family asked for the entire Coroner's Inquiry proceedings to be held in private, and the AGC will consider the request carefully.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The family even asked for the entire Coroner's Inquiry proceedings to be held in private.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Attorney General's Chamber (AGC) will give their request careful consideration.

sections.label: Coroner's Inquiries held in public
sections.summary: Coroner's Inquiries in Singapore are held in public unless the Court decides part should be private.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: All Coroner's Inquiries in Singapore are held in public, unless the Court decides that some part of it should be in private.

sections.label: Allegations before Coroner's Inquiry
sections.summary: Allegations about five officers, Police pressure and Benjamin's suicide may infringe sub judice principles and are improper before the Coroner's Inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The various pronouncements, suggestions, statements which imply and allege that five officers interviewed him, that the Police pressured and intimidated Benjamin into wrongly admitting to guilt and that these must have been amongst the reasons why he committed suicide; all these allegations possibly infringe the principles of sub judice, apart from being highly improper at this stage, prior to the Coroner's Inquiry.

sections.label: Police not responding to allegations
sections.summary: The Police were right not to respond, out of respect for the Coroner's Inquiry process.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Police, out of respect for the Coroner's Inquiry process, were right in not responding.

sections.label: Government decision to set out facts
sections.summary: Assertions on Police integrity and many Parliamentary Questions led the speaker, after consulting the AGC, to set out facts despite sub judice rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Assertions which go to the integrity of the Police Force have been repeated several times, including untrue factual assertions, and Members have filed many Parliamentary Questions (PQs).

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In these circumstances, not everyone will know why the Government has not responded and people may misunderstand if the Government did not respond.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Thus, I decided, with some regret, and considerable reservation, and after consulting the AGC, that we will have to set out the facts and discuss the matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The rules of sub judice generally preclude discussions which may prejudice proceedings, but public officials like myself can make statements if they believe it to be necessary in the public interest, even if there is a hearing pending.

sections.label: Discussions before hearings and precedent
sections.summary: Legitimate discussion of general principles before hearings must be done with care, the law will be relooked, and today's discussion should not become an automatic precedent.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Even prior to the hearings, there can be legitimate discussions on general principles and approaches but it has to be done with some care.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We will relook at the law to see how we can try and achieve this better.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The discussion today that we are having in the House should not become an automatic precedent for the future.

sections.label: Points addressed and every life matters
sections.summary: The speaker addressed the case facts, untrue statements about the Police, and the timing of discussion, concluding that every life matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I have addressed the following points today, Mdm Speaker.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I have outlined the facts of the case as we know them.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I have set out some of the untrue statements that have been made about the Police.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And I have explained why we had not seen it right to discuss this matter earlier and, at the same time, why at this stage, I decided that we will discuss it.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If I may say this in conclusion, Mdm Speaker, at the end of the day, every life matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It matters to the Police, it matters to the Government and it matters to all of us.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: After which, Madam, with your permission, we will both address clarifications that Members may want to seek.
